marble.name: Flat vs Solid Shapes
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Distinguish two-dimensional (flat) shapes from three-dimensional (solid) shapes
marble.prompt: Does you understand the difference between a flat shape like a square and a solid shape like a cube — and can they sort everyday objects into flat or solid?

cluster.summary: Your child is exploring shapes and space — recognising circles, triangles, and squares, building with 3D shapes like cubes and spheres, and describing where things are using words like above, below, and beside.

misconceptions: Applies a flat (2-D) name to a solid object — calls a ball 'a circle', a cube 'a square', a cone 'a triangle' (Mohamed & Kandeel 2023; Nurnberger-Haag).
Sorts by overall appearance as a whole rather than by dimensionality — groups the round ball with the round circle because both 'look round' (van Hiele visual level).
Confuses a drawing of a solid with the solid itself — treats a cube drawn on paper as 'solid' because of its name.
representations: Real objects to handle: ball, cube/box, tin, cone beside paper circle, square, triangle
The 'draw it vs hold it' test
authoredAnswer: Puts the paper circle and square with the flat shapes and the ball and cube with the solids; explains that the ball is solid because it is round in every direction and you can hold and turn it and it takes up space, whereas the circle just lies flat on the paper — so the ball is a sphere, not a circle.

wrongAnswers.wrong: The ball is round, so it is a circle — it goes with the flat shapes
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Names the solid with a 2-D word and places it in the flat group
wrongAnswers.fix: Hand the child the object to hold and turn: 'a circle is flat on the paper; the ball is round every way and you can pick it up — that is a sphere'; teach the twin-pair names

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Puts the ball with the circle 'because they both look round'
wrongAnswers.fix: Use the dimensional test on the mathematical shape represented: does it extend in three independent directions, or is it an ideal flat shape represented by a thin card? Both a card and a ball can be held and turned, so pick-up ability alone does not separate f

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Calls a picture of a cube 'solid' but cannot say the drawing itself is flat on the page
wrongAnswers.fix: Contrast the drawn cube (flat on the page, you cannot grasp its corners) with the real cube you can hold and turn

before.name: 2-D shapes
before.reason: Distinguishing 2-D from 3-D requires knowing what 2-D shapes are
